title: Proactive capacity shear and tenant fairness index
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: We observe repeated short-duration contention across dedicated pools where static reservations cause nearby tenants to either starve or overrun resulting in amplified autoscaler churn. This PR introduces a proactive 'capacity shear' mechanism that gradually rebalances reserved capacity between pools ahead of predicted demand spikes and a tenant fairness index (TFI) to guide reallocation decisions. Motivation: Reduce oscillation and emergency cold-starts by using decorrelated utilization signals and a fairness objective that accounts for recent latency targets, percentiles, and committed throughput. Design summary: 1) Capacity shear controller: a continuous controller (provisioner/shear.go) that computes candidate reallocations using multi-window utilization deltas and headroom forecasts. Shear actions are constrained by safety knobs: min_reserve_floor, per-tenant cooldown, and a circuit-breaker preventing >10% cap movement in a 5m window. 2) Tenant Fairness Index (TFI): a composite score computed from normalized committed throughput, 95th latency violations, and historical utilization elasticity. TFI is used as a weight when distributing reclaimed capacity. 3) Utilization demultiplexer: telemetry/util_demuxer.go ingests aggregated pool metrics and emits tenant-level signals by probabilistic attribution when direct counters are missing. 4) Telemetry and debugging: new metrics (shear_attempts_total, shear_applied_bytes, tfi_distribution, demux_confidence) + an ops endpoint (/debug/shear/state) for dry-run inspection. Rollout plan: opt-in flag per-pool (provisioner.features.capacity_shear=true). Start in dry-run mode for 48h, then enable gradual apply with safe limits set conservatively for the first week. Backout is a simple feature flag toggle. Testing and validation: extensive unit tests for controller math, integration tests in perf-canary using synthetic multi-tenant traces, and a staged canary rollout across 3 clusters. Observability: dashboard updated with time-series of TFI and per-tenant headroom; alerts added for shear_applied_rate > expected thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc linked || docs/design/capacity-shear.md [x] unit tests [x] integration canary harness [x] e2e perf validation [x] feature flag gating [x] ops runbook added. Impact and metrics to watch: decrease in emergency scaling events, reduction in median cold-start latency, and stable SLA compliance. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. Cost: small steady-state controller CPU + increased metric cardinality; we measured <2% infra cost bump in canary clusters.
